summary: Lunar Landing Navigator  is an interactive mission-planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to help students and aerospace enthusiasts explore lunar topography and evaluate spacecraft landing safety. Utilizing elevation profiles derived from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), the app provides interactive 2D maps and 3D terrain visualizations for historic touchdown locations like Apollo 11's Tranquility Base and Chandrayaan-3's Shiv Shakti Point, as well as Artemis polar targets. It  combines transparent, rule-based safety algorithms—assessing slopes, surface roughness, boulder fields, and solar illumination—with an integrated AI assistant that generates mission feasibility verdicts and descent mitigation strategies.
